newsitem.title: UK: Poll shows Labour lead slashed to five points.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows Labour lead slashed to five points.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives have reduced the opposition Labour Party's lead to just five points, according to an opinon poll released on Wednesday.
The ICM poll in The Guardian newspaper put Labour at 42 percent, the Conservatives at 37 percent and the Liberal Democrats at 14 percent.

"In a dramatic development, which may prove to be the definitive point in the 1997 election campaign, Labour's lead over the Conservative party has been reduced to just five points," the Guardian said in a statement.

The ICM poll, which has consistently given Labour a smaller lead than other polls, showed the Conservatives gaining six points, from 31 to 37 percent, since the previous week and Labour dropping three points from 45 to 42.
ICM used television interviews of a random sample of 1,004 adults on April 20 and 21 for the poll.

The Guardian poll contradicted a Gallup survey in The Daily Telegraph which showed the Labour Party had stretched its lead over the Conservative Party to 21 points, an increase of five, over the previous week.
